title: Gratitude Bar
overview: Architected and rebuilt the Gratitude Bar live event platform using AppSync GraphQL, DynamoDB, and WebSocket subscriptions, supporting 5,000+ concurrent users, increasing engagement by 264%, and reducing monthly cloud costs by about 80% through database and infrastructure redesign.
challenge: The primary challenge was to create an app that could represent a key aspect of our product in a quick, engaging, and digestible way at large-scale events. Previous versions of the app closely mimicked the product but lacked live, interactive elements, making it less engaging for attendees. The goal was to build an experience that truly captured the real-time, social nature of the product, encouraging attendees to interact more dynamically and feel a sense of immediate connection.
solution: To deliver a seamless and interactive experience, I leveraged modern tooling with Next.js and DynamoDB, integrating Amplify AppSync for WebSockets to enable real-time updates. When someone sends an award, it appears immediately in the awards feed. Attendees can send points to one another, and these transactions reflect instantly on the platform. A built-in raffle system incentivizes continued interaction, drawing users in to engage more frequently. By prioritizing real-time responsiveness, we created a highly engaging event experience that successfully embodied the spirit of our product.

title: Workhuman Live Orlando 2026
overview: Led migration of the Workhuman Live marketing platform from WordPress to headless Contentful and Next.js, improving Lighthouse performance from 49 to 99 and reducing load time by 86%.
challenge: For Orlando 2026, the challenge was bigger than launching another event site. We needed to support a growing registration target while also rethinking the underlying platform powering the Workhuman Live marketing experience. The legacy WordPress setup made it harder to achieve the level of speed, flexibility, and scalability needed for a flagship event, especially as content, design expectations, and business needs continued to grow. At the same time, the site still needed to feel premium, dynamic, and informative enough to convert visitors into attendees. Accessibility remained a key requirement throughout, alongside the need to support editorial agility and deliver on a tight event timeline. The challenge was balancing ambitious experience goals with the complexity and risk of a full platform transition.
solution: To address this, I led the migration of the Workhuman Live marketing platform from WordPress to a headless Contentful and Next.js architecture, creating a stronger foundation for both the Orlando event and future scalability. The approach centered on close collaboration across development, design, and content teams to translate the event vision into a reusable, component-based system that was both visually polished and technically sustainable. Contentful provided a more modular editorial model, while Next.js enabled a significantly faster and more performant frontend experience. Throughout the build, accessibility and usability remained core priorities, with attention to semantic structure, keyboard support, and inclusive patterns. This new architecture gave the team greater flexibility, improved maintainability, and dramatically elevated site performance, increasing Lighthouse from 49 to 99 and reducing load time by 86%.

title: Workhuman Live Denver 2025
overview: I collaborated closely with the design team to shape the Workhuman Live 2025 experience, ensuring functional and reusable components like filters, menus, and fixed elements. Leading the development team, I planned and assigned tasks to other developers, reviewing and integrating their work while mentoring them on the platform's unique features.
challenge: For the Denver event, our registration goal increased significantly, requiring a website that could engage and entice thousands of attendees to invest in the experience. We needed to level up the user experience from Workhuman Live Austin 2024, making the site more dynamic, visually compelling, and informative. Additionally, accessibility was a top priority, ensuring an inclusive experience for all users. We had to balance cutting-edge design with technical feasibility being in WordPress/PHP/jQuery, maintaining performance and flexibility while integrating new UX improvements.
solution: From the start, close collaboration between design and development was critical to ensuring the site's success. Development signed off on functionality and what was possible within our custom WordPress environment before designs were finalized. Regular feedback loops between design and dev allowed for continuous improvements, ensuring a polished, user-friendly experience. A stronger focus on WCAG compliance, keyboard navigation, and color contrast improvements made the site more inclusive than ever. Building with Advanced Custom Fields (ACF) allowed for modular content updates while maintaining design integrity. This structured, iterative approach resulted in a highly engaging event website that successfully met our goals, providing a visually compelling, accessible, and seamless experience for thousands of attendees.

title: Alt Text Generator
overview: I built and launched an AI-powered alt text generator that scaled accessibility support across Contentful and WordPress workflows for multiple marketing teams. Built with Next.js, AWS, Python, and OpenAI, the tool generates high-quality, brand-aware alt text directly within existing content workflows, reducing manual effort while improving consistency, accessibility, and SEO. The app was adopted across several internal teams and evolved into reusable tooling that could also be made available beyond its initial implementation.
challenge: Alt text was often missing, inconsistent, or manually written in ways that slowed content production and created accessibility gaps across marketing platforms. Existing approaches did not reliably capture Workhuman's brand voice, product context, or the nuances of different image types, making it difficult to scale quality standards across teams and workflows.
solution: I designed and implemented an AI alt text generator tailored to Workhuman's brand, content standards, and product imagery, enabling teams to create more accurate and accessible descriptions with minimal friction. To support different workflows, I delivered the solution through multiple integration paths, including embedded CMS experiences, a standalone interface, and API-based connectivity. This made the tool flexible enough to support several teams while improving adoption, consistency, and ease of use across platforms.

title: Workhuman Web Assistant
overview: I built an AI chatbot prototype designed to modernize website search through a conversational, content-aware experience. The frontend was developed in Next.js and TypeScript, while the AWS-based backend used Python and Node.js to ingest, process, and refresh website content on a recurring schedule. By combining automated knowledge base updates with OpenAI-powered responses, the prototype delivered more intuitive, accurate answers and guided users to relevant site content more effectively than traditional search.
challenge: Traditional site search made it difficult for users to quickly find the most relevant content across blogs, landing pages, and other website resources. The goal was to create a more natural discovery experience that could answer questions directly while also guiding users to useful content across the site. A key challenge was ensuring the chatbot stayed current as website content changed frequently, including regular blog publishing and page updates, while still maintaining accurate, fast, and contextually relevant responses.
solution: I designed and developed a conversational chatbot experience with a Next.js and TypeScript frontend and an AWS backend powered by Python and Node.js. To keep the experience current, I implemented an automated ingestion pipeline that refreshed the knowledge base on a recurring basis as site content changed. I also integrated OpenAI GPT-4o mini to generate site-specific responses, supported by content retrieval and session context to make interactions feel more natural and useful. The result was a highly interactive prototype that reimagined search as a guided conversational experience, helping users surface answers and navigate to relevant content more efficiently.
